title: What is the difference between a debit card and a credit card?
sources: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Regulation E vs Z

lines.text: Both cards swipe the exact same way at registers, but using a debit card carries vastly higher financial danger.
lines.caps: Why wealthy people *never | swipe a *debit card

lines.text: When you swipe a debit card, money is pulled instantly straight out of your personal checking account.
lines.caps: Debit pulls cash *straight | from your checking *account!

lines.text: If a gas pump skimmer steals your debit card info, a hacker drains your actual rent money before dinner.
lines.caps: A skimmer drains your *real | rent money in *seconds

lines.text: Federal regulations give you only limited liability protection if you don't report debit fraud immediately.
lines.caps: Debit fraud disputes can take *weeks | to recover your *cash

lines.text: With a credit card, you are spending the bank's money, not your own.
lines.caps: With credit, you spend the *bank's money | not your *own!

lines.text: If fraudulent charges occur, federal law caps your liability at zero dollars, and the bank fights to recover its funds.
lines.caps: Zero liability means *fraud | never touches your *savings

lines.text: Use credit cards for safety and rewards, but always pay off the balance in full every single month.
lines.caps: Use credit for *protection | and pay the balance *in full!
